fullPassage: Imagine you are pedalling your bicycle on a level road. You stop pedalling: no force is now acting to move you forward. What happens? You gradually slow down. How could you slow down more suddenly, in a shorter distance? By putting the brakes on. Because the brakes change your movement, making you slow down more suddenly, they must be exerting a force on the bicycle and you, as they grip and rub on the wheel-rims. This is the force called friction, which tends to slow down moving things by acting in the direction opposite to movement, that is backwards. Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces acting on you and your bicycle, which also slow you down. One of these is friction in the wheels rubbing on the axles. Another is air resistance, which you can feel, pushing you backwards as you and the bicycle move forwards. When you apply these ideas to something around you, like a cart, you can see what could be generating friction: mainly the axles rubbing on the body as they rotate.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) level=평평한, (B) opposite=반대의, (C) pushing=밀어내는
det.analysis:
❌ ① steep — opposite — pushing: (A) steep(가파른)은 level(평평한)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② level — similar — pushing: (B) similar(비슷한)은 opposite(반대의)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ③ level — opposite — pushing: 원문 일치. 평평한(level) 길을 달리고, 마찰은 운동과 반대(opposite) 방향으로 작용하며, 공기 저항이 뒤로 밀어낸다(pushing)는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ level — opposite — pulling: (C) pulling(끌어당기는)은 pushing(밀어내는)과 반대 방향이라 부적절
det.tip: a level road(평평한 길) / direction opposite to movement(운동과 반대 방향) / pushing you backwards(뒤로 밀어냄)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) gradually=점차, (B) exerting=가하는, (C) grip=붙잡다
det.analysis:
✅ ① gradually — exerting — grip: 원문 일치. 페달을 멈추면 점차(gradually) 느려지고, 브레이크가 힘을 가하며(exerting), 바퀴 테를 붙잡고(grip) 문지른다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② rapidly — exerting — grip: (A) rapidly(빠르게)는 페달을 멈춘 뒤 서서히 느려지는 맥락과 반대
❌ ③ gradually — removing — grip: (B) removing(제거하는)은 힘을 가하는 exerting과 반대 의미
❌ ④ gradually — exerting — release: (C) release(놓아주다)는 붙잡는 grip과 반대 동작
det.tip: gradually slow down(점차 느려지다) / exerting a force(힘을 가함) / grip and rub(붙잡고 문지름)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) tends=~하는 경향이 있다, (B) resistance=저항, (C) generating=만들어 내는
det.analysis:
❌ ① fails — resistance — generating: (A) fails(~하지 못하다)는 마찰이 물체를 느리게 하는 경향(tends)과 반대
❌ ② tends — momentum — generating: (B) momentum(운동량)은 뒤로 밀어내는 공기 저항(resistance)과 의미가 다름

det.tip: tends to slow down(느리게 하는 경향) / air resistance(공기 저항) / generating friction(마찰을 만들어 냄)

Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces acting on you and your bicycle, which also slow you down. One of these is friction in the wheels rubbing on the axles. Another is air resistance, which you can feel, pushing you backwards as you and the bicycle move forwards. When you apply these ideas to something around you, like a cart, you can see what could be generating friction: mainly the axles rubbing on the body as they rotate.
